headline: AI-written code is starting to find its own bugs
summary: Two things today: OpenAI upgraded its image model, and Vercel lets agents audit code for bugs.

items.title: OpenAI image model moves up to Images 2.6
items.pitch: OpenAI bumped its image generation model to Images 2.6, and it hit 322 points and 192 comments on HN the same day. A real time-saver for slides, reports, and cover images.
why: Official release with a lot of buzz on HN
Ready to use for slides, reports, and cover images
No coding needed, non-technical folks can pick it up
actions: Open the official release page, check the examples, and compare against what you usually make
deep_dive: It's just a new generation of OpenAI's image model, focused on output that's closer to a finished, usable image.
You can try it in whatever image tool you already use, but compare an old image first before switching your default.
I can't judge the actual improvement from the headline, so check the official examples and don't buy the hype yet.
items.signals: HN 322 points · 192 comments · OpenAI official release on 11-04

items.title: Vercel lets agents hunt for bugs in code
items.pitch: Vercel's agent scanned its own code around the clock, found 6,817 vulnerabilities, and fixed 1,411 of them. Free until November 10, so worth trying on that little AI-built tool of yours.
why: Finds issues and hands you patches, 1,411 already fixed
The free window only lasts until November 10
Catches the common bugs in AI-generated code
actions: Look for Security Reviews in the Vercel console, free before 11-10, and point it at a small GitHub project
deep_dive: It uses an agent to read the code and actually open the app to poke at it, hunting for places someone could break in.
Best for small web tools you vibe-coded; no use for Godot game projects.
The numbers are Vercel's own, so use the free version to see for yourself and don't treat it as foolproof insurance.
items.signals: @rauchg 839 likes · 6,817 bugs found / 1,411 fixed in 24h · free until 11-10
